projects.title: Robin
projects.subtitle: A gesture-based instrument for live performance

hero.image_alt: Robin custom physical instrument with copper touch pads and ESP32 microcontroller
hero.caption: Robin, a custom instrument for a live dialogue between performer and system.

projects.summary: Robin is a custom percussion instrument that turns touch and movement into a shared musical process between performer and system.
projects.project_thesis: The project asks how much of a musical performance can be controlled—and what new possibilities appear when the instrument makes choices of its own.
projects.visitor_experience: Touch sets rhythms in motion, while the performer's movement changes their pace and texture. The instrument introduces variation; the performer listens, responds, and shapes what happens next.

projects.title: A Machine for Misunderstanding
projects.subtitle: A text-to-sound experiment on communication and interpretation

hero.image_alt: A Machine for Misunderstanding modular synthesizer interface and 3D VAD vector visualization
hero.caption: A system that translates written language into modular sound.

projects.summary: A text-to-sound system and listening study exploring what changes when emotional language passes through a machine.
projects.project_thesis: When words are translated into sound, what carries through—and what is changed or misunderstood? The project explores this question through a machine-mediated exchange and a listening study.
projects.visitor_experience: Participants exchange short texts through a system that turns language into modular sound. One person sends a message; another listens to its sonic translation and describes what they hear. Comparing intention with perception makes each step of the exchange part of the work.

projects.title: Listener
projects.subtitle: Selective listening, repetition and place memory
projects.status: Interactive recordings available · Author texts in progress

hero.image_alt: Listener modular patch signal flow diagram with 249 modules in VCV Rack
hero.caption: The VCV Rack patch used to capture and repeat selected sound fragments.

projects.summary: Listener is a listening project built from recordings made in Nanjing. A VCV Rack patch selectively captures and repeats fragments of sound, exploring how a place can remain in memory through a few recurring sounds.
projects.project_thesis: How does listening become remembering when some sounds repeat and others fall away?
projects.visitor_experience: Explore Yihe Road, Deji Plaza, Jiuhua Hill and New City Plaza through their available images and recordings. Move between source audio and VCV recordings at the same elapsed time.

credits.role: Concept, Modular Patch Architecture & Sound Design
credits.name: Rex Li

projects.title: NYUSH Music Classifier
projects.subtitle: Comparing learned audio representations for genre classification

hero.image_alt: Confusion matrix from the held-out evaluation of an eight-genre music classifier
hero.caption: Held-out evaluation of the log-mel spectrogram classifier across eight FMA-small genres.

projects.summary: A music genre classification project developed for NYU Shanghai’s summer school, comparing three ways to represent audio for machine learning.
projects.project_thesis: Can learned audio representations help classify genres in a small, uneven dataset? The project compares MERT embeddings, log-mel spectrograms, and a statistical-feature baseline using the FMA-small dataset.
projects.visitor_experience: The pipeline converts music into features or spectrograms, then predicts one of eight top-level genres. In the reported held-out evaluation, the lightweight 2D CNN reached 29.2% accuracy. The confusion matrix makes the model’s uneven performance and genre overlap visible.

projects.title: Inner Landscape
projects.subtitle: A private music space for exploring how you perceive the world

hero.image_alt: Conceptual illustration of a room with a window, vinyl record, and listening figure
hero.caption: A room that grows from music, reflection, and the meanings a person chooses to share.

projects.summary: Inner Landscape is a private-first music-self project: a visual space that grows from the music a person shares, inviting them to explore how they perceive the world.
projects.project_thesis: Instead of treating playlists as taste data or asking an AI to explain a listener’s feelings, the project asks whether music can become a lens for self-understanding—and, later, a more meaningful way to connect with others.
projects.visitor_experience: Early prototypes explored playlist import and music-informed reflection. The design evolved toward a 2.5D room that starts quiet and gains color as music and writing accumulate. People can choose which facets to share, with privacy built into the social concept.
